name: open-in-ide
description: Adds a button for each source file Claude's replies mention (C++, C#, shaders, web, scripts, config) that opens it at the line in Rider, Visual Studio, VS Code or any editor you give a command for. Understands Unity and Unreal projects. (Windows only)

editor.title: Editor
editor.description: Which IDE opens the files (the /open-in-ide command overrides it). auto: the first of Rider, Visual Studio and VS Code that is running, else installed. custom: the Custom command below.

customCommand.title: Custom command
customCommand.description: The command line the custom editor runs, with {file}, {line}, {column} and {folder} (the session's folder) filled in, e.g. "C:\Programs\Notepad++\notepad++.exe" -n{line} "{file}". /open-in-ide custom <command> overrides it.

buttons.title: Button placement
buttons.description: Where the file buttons appear: paragraph (under the paragraph that mentions the file) or end (all at the end of the reply). /open-in-ide buttons overrides it.

riderPath.title: Rider executable
riderPath.description: Full path to rider64.exe. Leave empty to use the newest installed Rider.
